verdict.rationale: Babylon.js documents TypeScript support with full IntelliSense, and a user reports the TypeScript integration works well. The engine is consumed directly as a JS/TS library with a TypeDoc API reference, so the scripting language exposes the engine API. On the debugging side it ships a scene Inspector and the Spector WebGL debugger, but neither is evidenced as a script/code debugger (breakpoints, stepping); browser devtools are a host-platform capability and earn no credit. missing for 10: a first-party script-level debugger, explicit evidence that the full engine API is exposed to scripts, independent corroboration of the debugging workflow.

support.subject: As a game developer, the primary scripting language is productive and fully exposes the engine API, with a debugger behind it
